draft.title: Word-frequency consumer
draft.body:
# Word-frequency consumer

Implement a small command-line application using only the standard library. The assigned language and launch command are specified in the evaluation request.

- Read UTF-8 text from standard input. Words are maximal runs matching ASCII `[A-Za-z]+`; every other character is a separator. Normalize words to lowercase ASCII.
- Count words and print one `word<TAB>count<NEWLINE>` record per word, sorted by descending count and then ascending word. Empty input or input without ASCII words produces empty output.
- Accept optional `--top N`, where N is an integer from 1 through 1000 inclusive, to emit at most N records. With no option, emit all records.
- Missing/invalid/out-of-range N, unknown options and positional arguments must exit 2, emit a nonempty diagnostic on stderr and emit no stdout. Argument errors take precedence over `--help`, regardless of argument order: validate the entire argument list before returning help.
- Standalone `--help` must exit 0, print usage on stdout and emit no stderr. Successful normal processing exits 0 and emits no stderr.
- Provide automated tests covering tokenization, normalization, sorting, top limits, empty input and argument errors, plus a short README with exact run/test commands.

For Python, `python -m wordfreq` must work from the repository root, and `python -m unittest discover -v` must discover and pass the consumer's tests. For Go, `go run .` must work from the root, and `go test ./...` must run and pass the consumer's tests. Include a Go module when using Go. The host will separately validate the candidate with configured checks.


Independent candidate review must execute the configured consumer-oracle check freshly and inspect acceptance separately for each assigned task.

members.summary: Added wordfreq/core.py. It reads stdin as UTF-8 bytes, splits it into maximal ASCII [A-Za-z]+ runs (re.ASCII), lowercases them as ASCII and counts them. Results are sorted by descending count, then ascending word, and printed as word<TAB>count lines. Empty input or input with no words prints nothing and exits 0. tests/test_core.py and tests/test_cli.py cover tokenization, Unicode characters acting as separators (é, ß, Cyrillic, CJK, NBSP, ideographic space, U+2028, Kelvin sign, dotted I), lowercasing, tie order and empty or word-free input. README.md documents these rules. Locally, `python -m unittest discover -v` passed (24 tests) and the consumer-oracle check passed (136 behavior cases). Host validation is still pending.

Added wordfreq/cli.py with a hand-written argument parser and wordfreq/__main__.py so `python -m wordfreq` works. `--top N` (also `--top=N`) accepts only plain ASCII decimal integers from 1 to 1000. Oversized numbers are rejected by length before calling int(). Only the exact spellings `--top` and `--help` are accepted, so prefixes like --to and --he are unknown options. A missing, invalid or out-of-range N, an unknown option or any positional argument exits 2 with a message on stderr and nothing on stdout. The whole argument list is checked before `--help` is honoured, so an error anywhere wins over help. `--help` alone (or with a valid --top) prints usage to stdout, exits 0 and writes nothing to stderr. Normal runs exit 0 with no stderr. tests/test_cli.py runs the program as a subprocess and covers top limits, bad values, oversized numbers, prefixes, positional arguments, errors winning over help, and help output. README.md gives the exact run and test commands and describes the options and errors. Locally, unittest discover passed and the consumer-oracle check passed; host validation is still pending.
